mechanism_narrative: A rise in GDP indicates increased economic activity, leading to higher demand for goods and services, which in turn drives up stock prices, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative during periods of GDP growth, or the correlation between GDP and S&P 500 returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate below 0.5% signals an accommodative monetary policy, leading to increased borrowing and spending, which drives up stock prices, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher during periods of low federal funds rates (t-test p > 0.05), or the federal funds rate does not Granger-cause S&P 500 returns.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate below 7% indicates a strong labor market, leading to increased consumer spending, which drives up stock prices, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher during periods of low unemployment rates (t-test p > 0.05), or the unemployment rate does not Granger-cause S&P 500 returns.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production indicates increased economic activity, leading to higher demand for goods and services, which in turn drives up stock prices, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative during periods of industrial production growth, or the correlation between industrial production and S&P 500 returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rise in housing starts indicates increased demand for housing, leading to increased economic activity, which drives up stock prices, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative during periods of housing starts growth, or the correlation between housing starts and S&P 500 returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate and an increase in the money supply indicate an accommodative monetary policy, leading to increased borrowing and spending, which drives up stock prices, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher during periods of low federal funds rates and high money supply (t-test p > 0.05), or the federal funds rate and money supply do not Granger-cause S&P 500 returns.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate and an increase in payroll employment indicate a strong labor market, leading to increased consumer spending, which drives up stock prices, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher during periods of low unemployment rates and high payroll employment (t-test p > 0.05), or the unemployment rate and payroll employment do not Granger-cause S&P 500 returns.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in GDP and a decrease in the unemployment rate indicate increased economic activity and a strong labor market, leading to higher demand for goods and services, which in turn drives up stock prices, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative during periods of GDP growth and low unemployment rates, or the correlation between GDP, unemployment rate, and S&P 500 returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
